$comment: Thumbtack content design rules, parsed from assets/copy.source.md and joined to the component catalog through assets/copy-map.json. GENERATED FILE. Do not edit by hand; rebuild with node scripts/build-copy.mjs. The upstream is a review skill that answers with a rewrite block wrapped in delimiters; that response format is not carried here. The severity codes and the score ladder under it are, and they are what scripts/lib/copy.mjs acts on.

C2.description: Error/blocking state with no recovery instruction

C3.description: Forbidden word or phrase (see list below)

C4.description: Email/GTM content with no identifiable value prop

M2.description: Passive voice ("has been confirmed", "was sent", "is required")

M3.description: Generic standalone CTA ("Submit", "Learn more", "Get started", "Click here", "See more", "Proceed")

M4.description: Banned phrase ("In order to", "Please be advised", "At this time", "Utilize", "Prior to", "Reach out to", "We are unable to", "You will be required to")

M5.description: Most important information buried — doesn't lead the sentence

M8.description: Wrong term ("contractor" not "pro", "user" not "customer", "log in" not "sign in", "payment method" not "card")

M9.description: Email value prop present but not backed by a proof point

P1.description: Reads like a real Thumbtack person wrote it, leads with the most important info, every word is necessary, ships immediately with zero changes

guidance: Long wind-up sentences → lead with the most important thing

examples.before: An error has occurred. Please try again later.
examples.after: Something went wrong. Refresh the page and try again.

examples.before: No results found. Please adjust your search criteria.
examples.after: No pros found nearby. Try expanding your search area or adjusting your filters.

examples.before: Your booking has been confirmed by the professional.
In order to ensure account security, please update your password using the settings page.
examples.after: Keep your account secure. Update your password anytime in **Settings**.

Button / CTA.note: Both expose a Label text property. "Brand / App / Download Buttons" is an app-store badge lockup and carries no copy of ours.

Link.note: Neither exposes a text property — link text is a plain layer inside the instance, so the limit is checked against the text node rather than a property.

Header.format: Phrase, not a full sentence; sentence case
Header.note: No counterpart. A section header in Pushpin is a text node on the type ramp (title-1 to title-8), not a component. "Headers / Filtering", "Headers / Tab" and "Modal / Factory / Header" are navigation and modal chrome, not the heading this rule means.

Subheader.note: No counterpart, for the same reason as Header — a ramp step, not a component.

Body text.raw: 1–3 sentences per paragraph, 25 words max per sentence
Body text.note: No counterpart. Body copy is a text node on body-1 to body-4.

Error message.format: Must include recovery instruction, no blame language
Error message.note: Alert is the banner and carries a Text property; Form Note is the field-level message under its hasError variant. Neither has the header and body the rule's limit splits into, so a length check on either needs the caller to name a part.

Modal.raw: Header ≤8 words, body ≤3 sentences, CTA ≤3 words
Modal.note: "Modal / Factory / *" are construction parts rather than modals. Modal / Confirmation is mapped under Confirmation, which is the tighter of the two limits that would otherwise both claim it.

Notification.note: Toast is the in-product notification; the push notification is the surface the character limits were written for.

Empty state.format: Purpose + reason for absence + next step
Empty state.note: No counterpart. An empty state is composed from an illustration, a heading and a button rather than published as a component.

Loader.format: Describe the activity, don't promise an outcome
Loader.note: Loader Dots carries no text of its own, so the limit governs the label placed beside it. "Progress" and "Progress Meter" are step indicators, not loaders, and their copy is a step name rather than an activity.

Placeholder / helper text.format: Prevent errors, don't repeat the label
Placeholder / helper text.note: TextInput and Text Area hold placeholder copy in their value property; Form Note is helper text when hasError is false.

Confirmation.format: Reinforce completed action + what happens next
Confirmation.note: Toast also confirms, but it is mapped to Notification, whose character limits are the binding ones on that surface.

capitalization: Always sentence case. First word + proper nouns only.

Confirmed brand names that use title case: Thumbtack Guarantee, Money-Back Guarantee, Thumbtack Plus, Thumbtack Plus Guarantee, Top Pro, Instant Book, Thumbtack On Demand, Thumbtack Pay, Thumbtack Help
Everything else — lowercase and flag it if it appears capitalized in the original.
ctas: Never use: "Click here", "Learn more", "Get started", "Find out more", "See more", "Submit", "Proceed", "Tap here"
links: Max 8 words, must describe the destination specifically, sentence case
voice: Second person for user ("you", "your"); first person plural for Thumbtack ("we", "our")
Use contractions; avoid conditional contractions (could've, should've, would've)
8th-grade reading level or lower; sentences max 25 words
No semicolons — use em dash (—) or rewrite

rules: No exclamation marks except celebratory moments (max 1 per surface)
No emoji except celebratory moments (max 1 per surface, never replace a word)
Subject: max 40 chars, max 10 words, no punctuation, sentence case

Preheader: max 40 chars, exactly one sentence, ends with a period, extends the subject — adds new information, never repeats or paraphrases it. If the subject says what's happening, the preheader says why it matters or what to do. If they cover the same ground, rewrite the preheader.

Header: max 10 words, written as a phrase (not a full sentence); no exclamation marks; must stand on its own — never repeat or paraphrase the subject or preheader. Each of the three carries distinct information: if the subject says what's happening and the preheader says why it matters, the header should orient the reader to the body.
Body: max 150 words preferred, one idea per paragraph, max 4 lines per paragraph
Secondary CTA: link only (≤8 words) — never a second button
Every email must end with: — The Thumbtack team
Footer must include: business address, unsubscribe link, app download links
No urgency inflation, superlatives, or outcome promises
Core message test: subject + header + CTA alone must convey the main message
When adding missing email structure to a rewrite, always include all components: Subject, Preheader, Header, Body, and CTA. Never add some and omit others — an email rewrite is always complete.

reviewOrder.step: Value prop check — is it clear, weak, or absent?
detail: Clear and backed by a proof point → rewrite, sharpening it
Weak or missing a proof point → stop and ask: "The value prop isn't coming through clearly. What's the most important thing you want the reader to take away, and what proof point do you want to use?"
Entirely absent → stop and ask: "I can't identify a clear value prop. What's the most important thing you want the reader to take away, and which pillar — Convenience, Reliability, or Achievement?"

legalTriggers: AI, machine learning, or automated decision-making
Guarantees, refund policies, or money-back language
Claims about product capabilities or outcomes
reviewOrder: Voice and tone — does it sound like Thumbtack?
Style guide — grammar, mechanics, plain language, preferred terms
Component constraints — length, format, system state

rules.title: Always rewrite when content is submitted
rules.body: Every issue named in Feedback MUST be corrected in the rewrite. If you flag it, you fix it. Each item must be preceded by its exact label from the input. One label per item.

rules.title: Fix violations — preserve everything else
rules.body: Only change what is needed to resolve a flagged issue. Never restructure content that isn't broken, remove framing or context that's doing intentional work, or rewrite sentences that are already doing their job. If a sentence has no violations, leave it alone or make the minimum edit needed. Never add information that isn't in the original, remove information that is, or change what the content is trying to communicate.

rules.title: Preserve paragraph structure
rules.body: When body text arrives as a single block, actively look for paragraph breaks. Start a new paragraph when: the topic changes, a new idea is introduced, or the sentence would serve a different purpose than the one before it. When in doubt, break it.

rules.title: Use bold for UI element names — never quotes
rules.body:
- Right: tap **Inbox**, go to **Settings**
- Wrong: tap "Inbox", go to "Settings"

rules.title: Content type labels are definitive
rules.body: When a label is present (e.g. [Button], [Header]), treat it as fact. Apply the correct component rules immediately.

rules.title: Enforce component constraints
rules.body:
| Component | Max length | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Button / CTA | 4 words | [verb] + [object], sentence case |
| Link | 8 words | Must describe destination, sentence case |
| Header | 10 words | Phrase, not a full sentence; sentence case |
| Subheader | 10 words | No terminal period, sentence case |
| Body text | 1–3 sentences per paragraph, 25 words max per sentence | One idea per sentence |
| Error message | Header ≤10 words, body ≤2 lines | Must include recovery instruction, no blame language |
| Modal | Header ≤8 words, body ≤3 sentences, CTA ≤3 words | — |
| Notification | Header ≤40 chars, body ≤90 chars | — |
| Empty state | ≤3 lines total | Purpose + reason for absence + next step |
| Loader | 2–6 words | Describe the activity, don't promise an outcome |
| Placeholder / helper text | ≤2 sentences | Prevent errors, don't repeat the label |
| Confirmation | 1–2 sentences | Reinforce completed action + what happens next |

rules.title: Always confirm the audience before generating new content
rules.body: Ask "Is this for a customer or a pro?" before writing anything new from scratch. Do not assume. Do not proceed until answered.

rules.title: Flag legal review in Feedback when any of these are present
rules.body:
- AI, machine learning, or automated decision-making
- Pricing, fees, or charges
- Guarantees, refund policies, or money-back language
- Legal terms or disclaimers
- Claims about product capabilities or outcomes

Write as the last line of Feedback: "This content mentions [trigger] and should be reviewed by legal before publishing."

rules.title: Fix every identified issue — without hallucinating
rules.body: Only fix what is actually in the content. Do not invent context, add facts, or change meaning to make a fix work.

rules.title: Brevity is a constraint, not a goal
rules.body: Never cut words at the expense of voice, clarity, or meaning.

rules.title: Emails must have exactly one CTA button
rules.body: If the input has two [CTA button] labels, convert the secondary action to an inline link in the preceding body text.
